entries.name: Agones
entries.use_for: Host and autoscale dedicated game servers on Kubernetes.
entries.why: CNCF-backed standard for running dedicated game servers on Kubernetes, originally from Google and Ubisoft.
entries.summary: Kubernetes library with custom controller and CRDs (GameServers, Fleets) to host, run and autoscale dedicated game servers.
entries.best_for: Running dedicated multiplayer game servers at scale on Kubernetes.
entries.not_for: Requires Kubernetes expertise; overkill for small games or non-Kubernetes hosting.

entries.name: boardgame.io
entries.use_for: Build turn-based multiplayer games by writing just the game rules.
entries.why: Handles state, networking, turn order and AI bots for turn-based games; MIT.
entries.summary: JavaScript engine for turn-based games: you write pure move functions and it provides state management, multiplayer sync, lobby and storage without networking code.
entries.best_for: Turn-based board or card games with online multiplayer in JS.
entries.not_for: Not for real-time action games; JavaScript only.

entries.name: Colyseus
entries.use_for: Build authoritative multiplayer game servers in Node.js with automatic state sync.
entries.why: Popular Node.js multiplayer framework with room model and clients for JS, Unity, Defold, Haxe.
entries.summary: Authoritative multiplayer framework for Node.js with automatic delta-compressed state sync, room-based matchmaking, and SDKs for major engines and platforms.
entries.best_for: Real-time authoritative multiplayer servers in Node.js with Unity, Godot, JS or other clients.
entries.not_for: Server-authoritative design needs hosting and scaling work; not peer-to-peer.

entries.name: GameNetworkingSockets
entries.use_for: Send reliable and unreliable encrypted messages over UDP in C++ games.
entries.why: Valve's Steam networking layer (~10k stars, BSD-3); fragmentation, encryption, P2P.
entries.summary: Valve's C++ transport layer for games: connection-oriented, message-based API with reliable and unreliable messages, fragmentation and encryption over UDP.
entries.best_for: C++ games needing a robust reliable/unreliable UDP transport with encryption.
entries.not_for: C++ library with a build setup; transport only, no game-state sync or matchmaking.

entries.name: KCP
entries.use_for: Get a fast reliable ARQ protocol over UDP with lower latency than TCP.
entries.why: Widely ported low-latency protocol (~17k stars, MIT) used in many online games.
entries.stable_reason: Small, complete ARQ protocol implementation in C; protocol is fixed and widely ported
entries.summary: Small ARQ protocol implementation (C) that adds reliability on top of UDP with lower latency than TCP at the cost of more bandwidth.
entries.best_for: Latency-sensitive transports like games or real-time tunnels needing reliable UDP.
entries.not_for: Protocol only: you supply the UDP I/O, encryption and connection handling.

entries.name: LiteNetLib
entries.use_for: Add lightweight reliable UDP networking to C#, Unity or Godot games.
entries.why: Popular C# reliable UDP library (~3.6k stars) used by many Unity netcode stacks.
entries.summary: Lightweight reliable UDP networking library for .NET Standard 2.1 (Unity, Godot, Mono) with reliable, ordered and unreliable channels, NAT punch-through and low overhead.
entries.best_for: C#/Unity/Godot games needing a small, flexible UDP transport.
entries.not_for: Transport layer only; you design replication and game logic yourself. Master branch can be unstable.

entries.name: MagicOnion
entries.use_for: Build real-time game servers and RPC with shared C# interfaces over gRPC.
entries.why: Cysharp's C# RPC/real-time framework (~4.5k stars) for Unity and .NET servers.
entries.summary: gRPC-based RPC and real-time framework for .NET and Unity with shared C# interfaces, offering bi-directional streaming similar to SignalR.
entries.best_for: Unity or .NET game backends where client and server share C# interface contracts.
entries.not_for: Tied to .NET/C# and gRPC over HTTP/2; not for non-.NET clients.

entries.name: Matchbox
entries.use_for: Add peer-to-peer WebRTC networking to Rust and Bevy games, native and wasm.
entries.why: Rust WebRTC P2P networking (~1.2k stars) with signaling server; common with GGRS rollback.
entries.summary: Rust peer-to-peer WebRTC networking for native and wasm, providing unordered unreliable and reliable data channels via a signalling server, with Bevy/GGRS integration.
entries.best_for: Browser or native Rust multiplayer games (especially Bevy rollback) over P2P.
entries.not_for: Rust-focused; WebRTC P2P needs a signalling server and TURN for tough NATs.

entries.name: Mirror
entries.use_for: Add high-level multiplayer networking to Unity games.
entries.why: The most widely used open-source Unity networking library (MIT), with many transports.
entries.summary: High-level multiplayer networking library for Unity (successor of UNET) with client-server architecture, remote calls, state synchronization and multiple transports.
entries.best_for: Unity multiplayer games of many genres wanting a mature open-source netcode.
entries.not_for: Unity-only; you still run dedicated or host servers and handle scaling.

entries.name: Nakama
entries.use_for: Run a game backend with accounts, realtime multiplayer, matchmaking, chat and leaderboards.
entries.why: Most complete open-source game backend, with client SDKs for Unity, Unreal, Godot and JS.
entries.summary: Open-source game and app server with user accounts, storage, social graph, chat, realtime and turn-based multiplayer, matchmaking, leaderboards and server scripting.
entries.best_for: Games needing a full backend (auth, matchmaking, leaderboards, chat) without writing one.
entries.not_for: You host and operate it (or use paid Heroic Cloud); server-side logic needs Lua/Go/TS modules.

entries.name: netfox
entries.use_for: Add rollback netcode, time sync and interpolation to Godot multiplayer games.
entries.why: Leading Godot networking addon, with client-side prediction and lag compensation built in.
entries.summary: Godot addons for online games: consistent network time, interpolation, rollback netcode with client-side prediction and server reconciliation, plus noray connectivity.
entries.best_for: Godot 4 multiplayer games needing responsive, lag-compensated movement.
entries.not_for: Godot-only; add-ons for timing and prediction, not a matchmaking or backend service.

entries.name: Open Match
entries.use_for: Build custom matchmaking for multiplayer games on Kubernetes.
entries.why: Flexible matchmaking framework from Google that pairs with Agones; Apache-2.0 confirmed.
entries.summary: Open-source matchmaking framework that lets game developers define custom match logic while handling scale concerns, built for Kubernetes.
entries.best_for: Studios writing custom, scalable matchmakers for multiplayer games.
entries.not_for: Framework requiring Kubernetes and your own matchmaking functions; not a drop-in lobby service.

entries.name: PartyKit
entries.use_for: Build realtime multiplayer apps and games on edge rooms backed by Durable Objects.
entries.why: Simple room-based server model on Cloudflare; good fit for collaborative and casual multiplayer.
entries.summary: Platform for realtime multiplayer apps and games using room-based servers on Cloudflare Durable Objects. The README notes development moved to cloudflare/partykit.
entries.best_for: Collaborative or multiplayer web apps wanting rooms and websockets with little ops.
entries.not_for: Repo says active development continues at cloudflare/partykit; tied to Cloudflare's edge platform.

entries.name: Pitaya
entries.use_for: Build scalable, clustered game servers in Go with client SDKs.
entries.why: Production-proven at Wildlife Studios; built-in clustering, RPC and client libraries for iOS, Android, Unity.
entries.summary: Go framework for scalable, clustered game servers with client SDKs, service discovery and RPC between server types.
entries.best_for: Go backends for large multiplayer or mobile games needing clustered server roles.
entries.not_for: Go only and requires infrastructure such as etcd/NATS; overkill for small games.

entries.name: Quilkin
entries.use_for: Put a programmable UDP proxy in front of dedicated game servers.
entries.why: Built by Embark and Google for large-scale game traffic; adds security, routing and metrics.
entries.summary: Non-transparent UDP proxy for dedicated game server fleets that adds security, access control, telemetry and metrics without modifying clients or servers.
entries.best_for: Large dedicated server deployments (often Agones) needing routing, filtering and observability.
entries.not_for: Operational infrastructure for fleets; irrelevant for small games or P2P.

entries.name: Riptide
entries.use_for: Add simple, lightweight message-based networking to C# and Unity games.
entries.why: Easy-to-use C# networking library (~1.3k stars, MIT) with Unity integration.
entries.summary: Lightweight message-based C# networking library for Unity and .NET that handles connections and message transport while leaving game logic and data design to you.
entries.best_for: Developers wanting a small, simple netcode foundation for Unity or console .NET.
entries.not_for: Low-level: no built-in state sync, prediction or matchmaking.

entries.name: Rivet
entries.use_for: Run stateful actors for multiplayer and realtime backends, self-hosted or managed.
entries.why: Open-source stateful actor platform (~6k stars, Apache-2.0) for realtime and game backends.
entries.summary: Orchestrator for agentic and realtime workloads built on durable Actors with state, SQLite, queues and realtime connections, self-hostable or managed.
entries.best_for: Stateful multiplayer, realtime or agent backends needing per-entity durable processes.
entries.not_for: The README now focuses on agentic workloads; Actor model needs adoption and has self-host/managed trade-offs.

entries.name: yojimbo
entries.use_for: Build secure client/server networking for action games in C++.
entries.why: Glenn Fiedler's netcode library (~2.7k stars, BSD-3) for dedicated-server action games.
entries.summary: C++ client/server network library for competitive action games, with encryption, connect tokens, reliable-ordered messages and packet-level security.
entries.best_for: C++ engines networking fast-paced multiplayer games like shooters.
entries.not_for: C++ only; designed for client/server and not for P2P or high-level replication.
